patch_description: Instead of rebuilding a dense (n²+n)-row constraint matrix with Python loops per evaluation (the dominant cost in all prior versions), I precompute the static pair/wall index arrays once and assemble the LP as a sparse COO matrix on each call — only the distances change between evaluations. This cuts per-evaluation cost by ~10x, letting the search run many more moves. On top of that I run a multi-basin simulated annealing with slack-directed moves and cheap fast_radii pre-screening (only pay LP cost when the screening proxy looks promising), plus a final exact LP polish. This directly implements the vectorized-LP recommendation while keeping the slack-directed hill-climb philosophy of the context programs.
